lesson_title: Splitting the Fee and Spreading the Meme: Hyperbolas and Exponentials
hook_text: Two things that can never happen at five-a-side. Both are drawn on your graph as dashed lines.
clip_script: The indoor pitch costs two hundred and forty rand for the hour — fixed, however many players arrive. Two players? One-twenty each. Three? Eighty. Four? Sixty. Six? Forty. Twelve? Twenty. Watch the drop — massive at first, then tiny. From two to three players, everyone saves forty rand. From eleven to twelve, barely two. Now the two things that can never happen. Pack the pitch with more and more players and the share keeps shrinking — but it never reaches zero. Someone always pays something. And you can never split the fee among zero players. Not a small number — not a thing at all. Those two impossibilities are the two lines your curve leans towards and never touches: asymptotes. It is also why this graph never crosses the vertical axis. No y-intercept. None. Different story now. You make a meme in first period and send it to two friends. Each of them forwards it to two more. One, two, four, eight, sixteen, thirty-two — past a thousand by round ten. Crawl, crawl, crawl, DETONATE. And run it backwards: a half, a quarter, an eighth — halve forever and something always remains. So that curve tiptoes just above the bottom line and never lands. Same idea, opposite direction.
visual_style: An indoor five-a-side pitch filling with players as a rand-per-player counter falls and a hyperbola traces itself; then a phone screen where forwards branch two at a time while an exponential curve rockets up beside it.
mood: Street-smart, quick, a little dramatic on the detonation.
pacing: Rhythmic on the fee splits, a pause on 'zero players', accelerating hard through the doubling.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sketch both curves asymptote-first.
